liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Alabama Getaway** (1 review, 1 other source): Alabama Getaway into Promised Land is called proud and powerful, with unusual energy for songs often played; Healy's PA mix is way off for the first minute of Alabama Getaway [14][17]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Cassidy closes with a nice jam at the end [18]
- **West LA Fadeaway** (1 review): Phil plays heavy, booming bass lines throughout West L.A. Fadeaway [17]
- **Deal** (1 review): Deal features Jerry playing fuzzed-out solos as his big turn at the end [18]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): The pre-drums Scarlet>Touch>Fire is very energetic and tight, described as the meat of the show [18]
- **Touch Of Grey** (1 review): The Scarlet into Touch transition is sweet: Jerry starts it and Brent joins in memorably [20]
- **Don't Need Love** (1 other source): Jerry leaves after Fire and does not play on the Jam into Don't Need Love [14]
- **Throwing Stones** (1 review): Bobby laughs at himself after a dyslexic slip of the words in Throwing Stones [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-07-03.139105.pcm.sbd.miller.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 155 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1984-07-03.163309.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 146 min [10]
- **gd1984-07-03.nak301.suraci.dalessandro.77440.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 146 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [13]. Said about its sound: Audience recording where crowd noise is buried within the music rather than overwhelming it; reviewer calls it a masterpiece [26]
- **gd84-07-03.aud.willy.14909.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 148 min; rated 4.47/5 by 15 [2]

## Around the show

- Jerry left early in the second set, leaving Brent without company on stage after the Scarlet>Touch>Fire stretch [17]
- Starlight is a small outdoor amphitheater with lawn and pavilion, holding over 7000, with castle-style structures on the sides [21]
- Midwest summer 1984 crowds were wild, with a heavy Shakedown Street vending scene outside [21]
- Reviewer ranks this Scarlet>Touch>Fire possibly the best, above the 7/13 version, and also cites a great one from 8/30/85 [20]
- The venue's setup and vibe are compared to Pine Knob [21]
- Scarlet>Touch>Fire combinations are rare, and 1984-85 set lists are appreciated for creativity and oddball choices [23]
- Reviewer considers this probably their favorite show of the 1984 tour, citing the Scarlet/Touch/Fire/Don't Need Love run [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-07-03.139105.pcm.sbd.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > PCM [1]
- **gd1984-07-03.163309.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Stephen Thomas; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Stephen Thomas' Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 capsules > Sony D5M [10]
- **gd1984-07-03.nak301.suraci.dalessandro.77440.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Tony Suraci; Eugene D'alessandro; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: Nakamichi CM300's(with CP1 Caps/pointed)>Sony D5M(XLIIS)Location: FOB/DFC Stand at 7 Feet/Pointed at Stacks [13]
- **gd84-07-03.aud.willy.14909.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>MC>??>DAT>CDR [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1984-07-03 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1984-07-03-backstage-pass/) [30]
